chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya, both together, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hamza ibn al-Tayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
If two remained, one of the two would be the Divine Authority upon his companion.

key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: The Divine Authority or Proof of God; in Shia theology, this refers to the Imam who is God's proof upon creation — his existence is obligatory and his authority is binding
key_terms.بَقِيَ اثْنَانِ: If two remained — a hypothetical minimum scenario used to establish the absolute continuity of the hujja, even at the limits of human existence

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about the necessity of a Divine Authority (hujja) on earth at all times?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts that the earth can never be devoid of a Divine Authority (hujja). Even in the most extreme hypothetical scenario where only two people remain on earth, one of them would necessarily be the hujja over the other. This teaching is foundational to the Shia doctrine of the continuous necessity of an Imam — the principle that God's proof (hujja) must always exist among mankind to guide them and establish the case for God.
